title: Tensor cohomology segments and quantitative Tor bounds for a pro-etale triangle
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and $A$ an arbitrary commutative ring. Work on the small pro-etale site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with its constant sheaf of rings $A_Y$ and the unbounded derived category $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Use the K-flat derived tensor product [def-weil-derived-tensor] and cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $U\to V\to W\to U[1]$ be a distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]. For every degree-zero $A_Y$-module sheaf $N$ and every $i\in\mathbf Z$, its tensor image has an exact cohomology segment
$$
 \mathcal H^i(U\otimes_A^L N)\longrightarrow
 \mathcal H^i(V\otimes_A^L N)\longrightarrow
 \mathcal H^i(W\otimes_A^L N).
$$
If $U$ has Tor amplitude in $[a_U,b_U]$ and $W$ in $[a_W,b_W]$, where $a_U\leq b_U$ and $a_W\leq b_W$ are integers, then $V$ has Tor amplitude in
$$[\min(a_U,a_W),\max(b_U,b_W)].$$
In particular if both outside vertices have Tor amplitude in the same ordered interval $[a,b]$, the middle vertex has Tor amplitude in exactly that interval. Tor amplitude means the vanishing for every module sheaf in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]; no constructibility or finiteness assumption on the coefficient ring or the vertices is imposed.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary degree-zero $A_Y$-module sheaf $N$. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the ringed site $(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_Y)$ to $N[0]$, obtaining a quasi-isomorphism $P\to N[0]$ with $P$ K-flat and every term flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated], $K\mapsto K\otimes_{A_Y}P$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and descends to an exact functor $T_P$ on $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, together with its shift comparison $T_P(K[1])\cong T_P(K)[1]$. Compare $T_P$ with the tensor of [def-weil-derived-tensor], which resolves the first argument: for a complex $K$ choose, again by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], a quasi-isomorphism $P_K\to K$ with $P_K$ K-flat with flat terms; by [lem-weil-derived-tensor-resolution-independent], $K\otimes_A^LN$ is $P_K\otimes_AN$ up to canonical isomorphism, whatever K-flat resolution was chosen. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated] to the fixed argument $P_K$ shows that $P_K\otimes P\to P_K\otimes N$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and applying it to $P$ shows that $P_K\otimes P\to K\otimes P$ is one. Hence $K\otimes_A^LN\cong T_P(K)$ in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for every $K$, and $T_P$ supplies the tensor image $K\mapsto K\otimes_A^LN$ on morphisms. Therefore the given distinguished triangle is sent to a distinguished triangle with vertices $U\otimes_A^L N$, $V\otimes_A^L N$, $W\otimes_A^L N$, and the shift comparison of $T_P$ identifies its last vertex with $(U\otimes_A^L N)[1]$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to the distinguished triangle of step 1 in the abelian category of $A_Y$-module sheaves. Its cohomology functors are the cohomology sheaves of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. In each integer degree $i$, the long exact sequence contains the exact segment $\mathcal H^i(U\otimes_A^L N)\to\mathcal H^i(V\otimes_A^L N)\to\mathcal H^i(W\otimes_A^L N)$. This proves the first assertion for every $N$ and $i$.

proof.text: Put $c=\min(a_U,a_W)$ and $d=\max(b_U,b_W)$. We have $c\leq a_U\leq b_U\leq d$, so $[c,d]$ is ordered. If $i<c$, then $i<a_U$ and $i<a_W$; if $i>d$, then $i>b_U$ and $i>b_W$. Thus, for every test sheaf $N$, both outside terms of the exact segment in step 2 vanish by the two Tor-amplitude hypotheses and [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Exactness then forces its middle term to vanish: the map from zero has image zero, while the map to zero has kernel the whole middle sheaf, so that sheaf is zero. This holds for every $N$ and every $i\notin[c,d]$, which is precisely the Tor-amplitude condition for $V$ in $[c,d]$.

source.place: Tag 08G2, lemma-cone-tor-amplitude (2), and Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude (1); enlargement to minimum/maximum is elementary.

proof.text: If $a_U=a_W=a$ and $b_U=b_W=b$, then $c=\min(a,a)=a$ and $d=\max(b,b)=b$. Step 3 therefore gives Tor amplitude in the same ordered interval $[a,b]$, as asserted. This is an interval of vanishing, with no assertion that its endpoints are optimal. All preceding steps quantified over arbitrary module sheaves and used no constructibility, boundedness of the vertices, or finiteness of $A$.
